definitions.explanation: Describes someone who gets angry easily and often. Built from {怒|おこ}る (to get angry) plus the suffix 〜っぽい, which marks a tendency, so it points at a habit rather than a single outburst.

examples.japanese: {寝不足|ねぶそく}だと{怒|おこ}りっぽくなる。
examples.english: I get irritable when I haven't had enough sleep.

examples.japanese: {怒|おこ}りっぽい{上司|じょうし}の{下|した}で{働|はたら}くのは{疲|つか}れる。
examples.english: Working under a short-fused boss is exhausting.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}{怒|おこ}りっぽくなったと{妻|つま}に{言|い}われて、{少|すこ}し{反省|はんせい}している。
examples.english: My wife told me I've become short-tempered lately, and I'm reflecting on it a bit.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
- {怒|おこ}りっぽい{人|ひと}: a quick-tempered person
- {怒|おこ}りっぽくなる: to become irritable (often about a temporary state — tiredness, illness, age)
- {怒|おこ}りっぽい{性格|せいかく}: an irritable disposition

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {気|き}が{短|みじか}い: short-tempered — the same trait stated as an idiom; slightly more neutral in tone
- {短気|たんき}: short temper — the noun, used in {短気|たんき}を{起|お}こす (to lose one's temper)
- {怒|おこ}りやすい: easily angered — plainer and more clinical; 〜っぽい carries a hint of criticism

USAGE:
Because it sounds mildly critical, speakers rarely apply it to a superior's face; it is normal in describing oneself or a family member.

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {怒|おこ}りっぽくなかったら
